subject: GEOGRAPHY
description: ICSE 10th Geography: Monsoon Mechanism, Western Disturbances, Alluvial, Black, Red and Laterite Soils

questions.question: Which branch of the South-West Monsoon brings heavy rainfall to Mumbai and Western Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats first, causing intense orographic precipitation.

questions.question: Which soil type is known as 'Regur Soil' and is ideally suited for cotton cultivation?
questions.explanation: Black soil is clayey, moisture-retentive, rich in minerals, and widely known as Regur/Black Cotton Soil.

questions.question: Winter rainfall in north-western plains (Punjab and Haryana) is primarily caused by:
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances originating over the Mediterranean Sea bring vital winter rain for Rabi crops.

questions.question: Which soil is formed as a result of intense leaching under heavy rainfall and alternating wet/dry seasons?
questions.explanation: Laterite soil forms due to leaching where silica and lime wash away, leaving iron and aluminium oxides.

questions.question: What is the localized pre-monsoon thunderstorm in West Bengal called?
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi (Calamity of the month of Baisakh) refers to evening thunderstorms in Bengal.
